label: models/fw_pipejunction.mdl: two pipes meeting at a flanged elbow, bolted

measured.lineup: ours is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/hvr.mdl, models/big_rock.mdl, models/crystal.mdl: the judge does not know which

M1.reason: Every view reads as the brief asks: a vertical pipe and a horizontal pipe meeting at a curved elbow, with a flange at each end of the elbow. Front, left, right, back and the four angled views give a clean L outline. Nothing sticks out except a small support block under the horizontal run, which suits the subject.

M2.reason: The brief gives no size, so nothing is measured against it. At 55 x 17.1 x 60 units the pipes are about 17 across and the whole thing is waist-to-chest high, a sensible size for a pumping-station prop.

M3.reason: Everything the brief names is there: two pipes, an elbow, a flange at both ends of the elbow (the joint to the vertical pipe and the joint to the horizontal pipe), and a ring of bolt heads on each flange. The bolts show in front, back, below and the angled views. The vertical pipe's top end has a rusted cap flange and there is a rusted support block under the horizontal run. Both are reasonable additions.

M4.reason: The pipes are grey-green painted steel and the flanges, cap and block are rusted brown steel, which fits the brief's 'rusted steel' and its Half-Life palette. Nothing is neon or sci-fi.

M5.reason: Yellow-black hazard bands sit on both pipes, rust streaks show on the pipe bodies (left, back and back-right views), and the flanges and block have a pitted rust texture. The bolts are crisp. The markings are sharp and in sensible places.

M6.reason: In the lineup it is C, the only industrial prop. Its texture density, low-resolution painted look and muted palette sit close to the game's own (hvr, big_rock, crystal at the same scale). A player would take it for a Half-Life pipe prop. The bright white bolt heads are a little clean but do not break the look.

M7.reason: It is upright, with the vertical pipe rising and the horizontal pipe and support block resting on the base plane. The front shows the elbow flange face-on with the pipe running away, a sensible front. Nothing is tilted or upside down.

M8.reason: SMAK's check passes with no errors, and nothing is open, inside out or floating: the horizontal pipe rests on the block. But it has 568 triangles against a Half-Life median of 105 for its size, which is 5.4 times the median and well past the cap of 2x (210). The bolts and round flanges are the likely cost.
